stories.notes: Complex multi-market (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature with zero acceptance criteria. Needs openspec first to elaborate requirements, define ACs, propose technical depth and potential story splits. Then speckit to harden with testability criteria, security checks (draft content exposure, auth for preview), and edge cases (multi-market rendering, concurrent edits, performance).

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — no Contentstack live-preview SDK wiring exists in the shown code. The attachment point is useContent (236 callers), which is the single funnel for all content fetching. Integrating the Live Preview SDK there automatically extends preview support to every existing consumer without modifying callers. App-level initialization (SDK config + root re-render wiring) is also required but the hook is the functional integration point.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array but a valuable architectural note identifying useContent (236 callers) as the single funnel and ContentstackContext as the app-level initialization point. I built the full AC list from that insight. Key additions: (1) AC-4/AC-5 cover error-handling edge cases (SDK init failure, connection loss) that openspec's note didn't address. (2) AC-6 covers security — preventing unauthorized access to draft content. (3) AC-7 ensures backward compatibility for all 236 existing consumers. (4) AC-8 ensures ContentstackLink preserves preview sessions during navigation. (5) AC-9 ensures ContentstackContext exposes preview state observably. (6) AC-10 ensures multi-content-type coverage, not just one. (7) AC-11 covers the draft-to-published transition edge case. (8) AC-12 covers mid-session activation. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I could not review the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, or ContentstackContext.tsx — the criteria are based on the story title, description, and file paths alone. The implementation team should validate that these criteria align with the actual code structure, especially around how ContentstackContext exposes state and how ContentstackLink constructs URLs.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the architectural integration points (useContent as the 236-caller funnel, ContentstackContext for app-level init), while speckit built a comprehensive 12-AC set covering error handling, security, backward compatibility, navigation, observability, multi-content-type coverage, and edge cases. However, speckit explicitly states it could not review the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, or ContentstackContext.tsx — all ACs are derived from the story title, description, and file paths alone. This is a material risk: the criteria may not align with actual code structure, especially around how ContentstackContext exposes state and how ContentstackLink constructs URLs. Additionally, both agents report acceptanceChanged=false despite the story starting with zero acceptance criteria and speckit authoring 12 ACs in its notes — the ACs may not have been persisted to the story's acceptanceCriteria array, which remains empty. Human review should validate (1) that the 12 ACs are actually written into the story record, and (2) that the ACs align with the real code structure of the identified files.
